questions.question: A Snowflake virtual warehouse is best described as which of the following?
options: A physical data center that stores all your tables and indexes persistently
A named cluster of compute nodes that executes queries and DML without owning storage
A logical container that groups databases, schemas, and tables under one account
A managed service that auto-scales persistent storage based on query volume
questions.explanation: A virtual warehouse in Snowflake is a named MPP compute cluster. It executes queries and DML operations but does not own or store data — all data lives in Snowflake's centralized cloud storage layer, keeping compute and storage independently scalable and billable.

questions.question: Snowflake's architecture separates which three distinct layers?
options: Ingestion, transformation, and serving layers
Bronze, silver, and gold data quality tiers
Storage, compute (virtual warehouses), and cloud services layers
Source, staging, and target database layers
questions.explanation: Snowflake uses three decoupled layers: (1) Cloud Services — the global brain handling metadata, security, query optimization, and transactions; (2) Query Processing — virtual warehouses that run queries; and (3) Database Storage — columnar micro-partition storage billed separately from compute.

questions.question: In Snowflake's role-based access control (RBAC) model, which statement best describes a role?
options: A role is an individual user credential used to authenticate sessions in Snowflake
A role is a named collection of privileges that can be granted to users or other roles
A role defines the cloud region where a virtual warehouse executes queries
A role is a network policy that restricts inbound connections by IP address range
questions.explanation: In Snowflake RBAC, a role is a named entity that holds privileges on securable objects such as databases, schemas, tables, and warehouses. Roles are granted to users or to other roles, forming a hierarchy. Users activate a role in a session to exercise its privileges.

questions.question: When executing a COPY INTO <table> command in Snowflake, which elements are always required?
options: A running X-Large warehouse and a pre-defined file format object in the schema
A named internal or external stage (or inline cloud storage path) and a destination table
An active Snowpipe configuration and an SQS or Event Grid notification channel
A TASK scheduler with a CRON expression and a stream on the source table
questions.explanation: COPY INTO requires at minimum a source location — a named stage such as @my_stage or an inline cloud URL like s3://bucket/path/ — and a destination table. File format can be inferred or defaulted; warehouse size has no minimum requirement; Snowpipe and Tasks are separate, optional features.

questions.question: What is the primary performance benefit of defining a cluster key on a large Snowflake table?
options: It enforces uniqueness on the key columns and prevents duplicate rows from loading
It compresses micro-partitions by deduplicating repeated values in the key columns
It co-locates related values in adjacent micro-partitions so fewer partitions are scanned per query
It distributes data evenly across active virtual warehouses to maximize parallel load throughput
questions.explanation: Snowflake stores data in immutable micro-partitions. A cluster key causes Snowflake's Automatic Clustering service to reorganize data so rows with similar key values land in the same or adjacent micro-partitions. Queries filtering on the cluster key can then prune most micro-partitions, dramatically reducing scan cost on large tables.

questions.question: Which Snowflake column type is designed to store a JSON document with a variable or unknown schema?
options: TEXT with a maximum declared length of 16,777,216 characters
OBJECT, which enforces a fixed list of named key-value pairs at the column level
VARIANT, which stores up to 16 MB of semi-structured data per value in a self-describing format
ARRAY typed as VARCHAR to serialize JSON as a delimited string column
questions.explanation: VARIANT is Snowflake's universal semi-structured type. It can hold JSON, Avro, ORC, Parquet, or XML data up to 16 MB per value. Snowflake stores VARIANT columns in columnar micro-partitions and supports querying nested paths with dot notation or the FLATTEN table function — no predefined schema required.

questions.question: A Snowflake table was accidentally dropped 30 minutes ago. Which built-in feature lets you recover it without opening a support ticket?
options: Fail-safe, which retains dropped-object data for 7 days after the Time Travel period ends
Time Travel, which lets you UNDROP the table or query its historical state within the retention window
Zero-copy cloning, which automatically preserves a shadow copy of every object on creation
Cross-region replication, which continuously mirrors a read-only replica to a secondary region
questions.explanation: Snowflake Time Travel lets you run UNDROP TABLE <name> to restore a dropped table (or schema or database) within the configured retention period (1 day on Standard; up to 90 days on Enterprise). Fail-safe is a subsequent 7-day window managed solely by Snowflake for disaster recovery — it is not accessible via SQL commands.

questions.question: An organization wants to give a business partner live, read-only access to specific tables without copying data or building ETL pipelines. Which Snowflake feature is the correct solution?
options: External tables pointing to a shared S3 bucket that both accounts can read concurrently
Snowflake Secure Data Sharing, which grants the consumer account access to a SHARE object containing selected database objects
Snowpipe streaming that continuously pushes CDC updates to the partner's Snowflake account
A database replication group that clones and synchronizes the full database nightly
questions.explanation: Secure Data Sharing lets a provider create a SHARE object containing specific tables, views, or other objects and grant it to consumer Snowflake accounts. Consumers see live data with no data copy, no storage cost to the consumer, and no ETL. External tables, replication, and Snowpipe serve entirely different use cases.

questions.question: Which virtual warehouse parameter suspends the warehouse automatically after a configurable idle period, minimizing unnecessary credit consumption?
options: MAX_CLUSTER_COUNT, which caps the number of active clusters during high-concurrency periods
AUTO_RESUME, which starts a suspended warehouse the moment a query is submitted against it
AUTO_SUSPEND, which suspends the warehouse after the specified number of idle seconds
STATEMENT_TIMEOUT_IN_SECONDS, which terminates long-running queries before they exhaust credits
questions.explanation: AUTO_SUSPEND (default 600 seconds) automatically puts the warehouse into a suspended state after it has been idle for the specified interval. A suspended warehouse consumes no compute credits. AUTO_RESUME controls restart behavior; MAX_CLUSTER_COUNT controls multi-cluster scaling; STATEMENT_TIMEOUT_IN_SECONDS limits individual query duration.

questions.question: Snowflake credits are primarily consumed by which of the following activities?
options: Storing data in internal named stages and returning rows from the query result cache
Running virtual warehouses, Snowpipe ingestion, and serverless features like Automatic Clustering
Network egress within the same cloud region and reads from external tables on public storage
Creating databases, schemas, and empty tables regardless of query or load activity
questions.explanation: Snowflake credits measure compute consumption. They are charged when a virtual warehouse is running (per-second billing per cluster), when Snowpipe processes files, and when serverless features such as Automatic Clustering, Materialized View maintenance, or Search Optimization run. Storage is billed separately in TB/month. DDL operations and result-cache reads consume no credits.
